question: What was the average fare BOS–LAX by quarter?
answer:
**Answer**

This is an ad hoc result from the DOT Consumer Airfare Report, Table 1a. It gives the average one-way fare for the BOS–LAX airport pair. The latest quarter, 2026 Q1, is $345.59. The table below shows the last 13 quarters.

| Year | Quarter | Avg one-way fare ($) | Passengers/day | Largest carrier (share) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026 | 1 | 345.59 | 2,425.74 | B6 (0.3148) |
| 2025 | 4 | 375.7 | 2,957.2 | B6 (0.3587) |
| 2025 | 3 | 361.82 | 3,105.03 | B6 (0.4024) |
| 2025 | 2 | 363.31 | 3,388.24 | B6 (0.402) |
| 2025 | 1 | 327.51 | 2,464.56 | B6 (0.4365) |
| 2024 | 4 | 351.7 | 3,466.74 | B6 (0.374) |
| 2024 | 3 | 337.94 | 3,630.33 | B6 (0.3849) |
| 2024 | 2 | 388.17 | 3,360.77 | B6 (0.3641) |
| 2024 | 1 | 357.96 | 2,571.87 | B6 (0.3675) |
| 2023 | 4 | 387.62 | 3,153.48 | B6 (0.4037) |
| 2023 | 3 | 365.79 | 3,545.87 | B6 (0.3437) |
| 2023 | 2 | 415.61 | 3,272.2 | B6 (0.3314) |
| 2023 | 1 | 335.86 | 2,606.11 | B6 (0.3674) |

**Why**

- The fare is seasonal. Q1 is the lowest quarter each year (2023 Q1 335.86, 2025 Q1 327.51) and Q2 or Q4 is usually higher.
- The query returned 100 quarters, from 2001 Q2 to 2026 Q1. I show only the recent ones here.
- Over that history, the 2022 Q2 fare (436.55) is the highest of the returned quarters I looked at, and 2004 Q2 (195.94) is among the lowest. In 2022 Q2 the largest carrier was DL (0.3122).
- JetBlue (B6) has been the largest carrier in every quarter shown since 2023, with a share between 0.3148 and 0.4365. UA is the low-fare carrier in most of those quarters. Its fare in 2026 Q1 was 291.81.

**Assumptions & scope**

- I read "BOS–LAX" as the airport pair, matching both orders (BOS–LAX and LAX–BOS). The city-pair market (Table 6) would be a different series.
- The query hit the 100-row limit, so older quarters before 2001 Q2 may exist but were not returned. All 100 returned quarters are distinct, one row each.
- Fares are average one-way fares from the DB1B 10% ticket sample. Only the largest domestic markets are published.
- Values are rounded to 2 decimals by the source. This is a Live Signal and never changes an Investment Opportunity Score.

**Data Confidence:** Medium. The query is ad hoc and outside the scoring methodology, and the data come from the DB1B 10% ticket sample. Source: DOT Consumer Airfare Report Table 1a (tfrh-tu9e), As-of Date 2026 Q1, window 100 quarters, 2001 Q2–2026 Q1.
